help.title: Help
help.intro: LabelBench designs a label, checks it, and prints it from this workstation. The notes below cover most of it.
help.step.model: Choose the printer model and the label size. The model decides which sizes are on offer, and the size decides how big the canvas is.
help.step.objects: Add the objects: text, images, codes, a date, a serial number.
help.step.variables: Mark the values that change per label, so a batch can fill them in.
help.step.check: Run the preflight check and fix what it reports.
help.step.save: Save the template to the server.
help.step.print: Print it, or run a batch.
help.toolbar_body: The controls are grouped, so what a button does is clear from where it sits.
help.toolbar_model_desc: Which printer this template is for. It decides the label sizes on offer.
help.toolbar_label_desc: The label's size, shape, print direction and tail.
help.toolbar_edit_desc: Undo, redo, the grid, and this help.
help.toolbar_add_desc: Text, icons, images, QR and barcodes, dates and serial numbers.
help.toolbar_templates_desc: Save a template to the server, or open one that is already there.
help.toolbar_data_desc: The CSV data source, and the batch run that prints from it.
help.toolbar_output_desc: The preflight check, the print preview, and the print itself.
help.canvas_body: The label is drawn on the workbench, in the shape it was given. The red edge is where the print starts. Zoom with the control in the corner: out, in, and fit — fit scales the label to fill the space it has, which is how you work with a 12 mm label on a large screen. The magnification is for editing only: what gets printed is unchanged.
help.preflight_body: Everything that would make the printed label wrong: text that overflows, text too small to read, low contrast, an object that runs off the label, text covered by another object, an empty text object, and a variable that was never filled in. Click a finding to select the object. The objects that run off the label can be put back with one button.
help.templates_body: A template lives on the server, not on this computer. Saving puts it there, and every workstation sees it at once — there is nothing to copy. The gallery lists everything on the server, and a template with no values in it prints straight from there.
help.printing_body: Printing happens in this browser, straight to the printer. The server never talks to a printer, so the printer has to be plugged into the workstation you are sitting at. Web Bluetooth and Web Serial only work on a page served over HTTPS, which is why the app is served from a trusted certificate.
help.serial_body: A date or a serial number is a token. The canvas shows what it looks like now, but the template keeps the token, so every copy of the label differs. The serial number comes from a counter on the server, so two workstations printing at the same time never get the same number. Select the serial number object to set its counter, prefix, suffix, start, step and padding.
editor.label_props: Label size, shape and print direction
help.shape_body: A label can be a rectangle, a rounded rectangle or a circle. The shape is how the label is drawn on screen and how it appears in the gallery and in the saved preview. It does not change what the printer burns: a roll printer lays dots onto whatever paper is loaded, and the paper outside the shape is simply white. Set the shape to match the label stock you actually use.
help.printers_body: One family of printer is supported: the NIIMBOT — the D11 or the B21 — reached over Bluetooth or over a USB serial adapter, and chosen in the app bar. The printer has to be plugged into the workstation the browser is running on: the server never talks to a printer.
help.batch_body: A batch prints one label per row of a CSV. The template declares its variables with {placeholders}; the CSV's columns are matched to them, and the mapping is saved with the template, so the same CSV works on every workstation. Every row can be previewed before anything is printed, and a row that fails is recorded with its reason while the rest of the batch carries on.
params.link.label: Link to object
params.link.hint: The barcode is encoded from the linked object, so it follows a serial number as the number changes.
params.rotate90.hint: Turn the object a quarter turn, to set it on its side.
help.objects_body: What you can do to an object once it is on the canvas.
help.objects_link_desc: A barcode or QR can follow another object — a serial number, a date, or a text box. It is then encoded from whatever that object holds when the label is printed, so the bars and the text always carry the same number.
help.objects_rotate_desc: Turns the object a quarter turn about its own centre, so it stays where it is on the label and only its direction changes. Use it to set something on its side.
help.objects_copy_desc: Ctrl+C copies the selected object and Ctrl+V pastes it a little to the side. Ctrl+Shift+C copies the text the object carries and Ctrl+Shift+V pastes text into it. The four buttons in the properties panel do the same.
params.scale.hint: Make the object bigger or smaller, keeping its shape and its place on the label.
preflight.auto_fix.hint: Move the objects that run off the label back inside it.
preflight.fixed_moved: {count} object(s) moved back inside the label
preflight.fixed_scaled: {count} object(s) made smaller to fit the label
preflight.fixed_none: Everything already fits inside the label
editor.print.hint: Open the preview. The number of copies and the other settings are there, and the print starts when you approve it.
help.objects_resize_desc: A corner handle resizes the object and keeps its shape. On a barcode that matters: bars stretched sideways are bars that will not scan. The two buttons beside it make the object bigger or smaller about its own centre.
help.preflight_fix_desc: The check finds the objects that run off the label and will be clipped. This button moves them back inside it, and makes an object smaller when it is too big to fit at all.
